messages:
nina: FYI presales ask from Meridian Bank — they want committed capacity guidance. Target: sustained 1800 qps chat (interactive) with p95 gen <250ms. Also heavy embedding lookups during peak (up to 600 qps). Thoughts on reserved pool + autoscale?
harry: Do we know token distribution? Interactive chat often has many short responses but spikes can hit 300+ tokens. p95 <250ms for gen is doable but depends on model choice.
zara: Customer leans to a 6B quantized family for primary, 13B as a higher-quality fallback for specific flows. That affects GPU efficiency heavily.
omar: Quick calc: assuming 6B quantized, one modern GPU handles ~280 qps with minimal batching. For 1800 qps baseline that's ~7 GPUs. Embeddings can be routed to CPU/embedding service or offload to separate instances; if on GPUs, add 2 GPUs.
lucas: I'd recommend baseline reserve 9 GPUs (7 for chat + 2 for embeddings), plus a small burst allowance of 3 GPUs for AZ failure and short spikes. Router policy should prefer reserve pool, overflow to burst credits.
nina: Customer asked for cost scenario comparison: fixed-reserve (12 GPUs) vs conservative-reserve (9 GPUs) + burst credits. Also wants SLA implications per option.
harry: For SLA: fixed 12 GPUs gives more headroom and simpler SLO guarantees. Reserve 9 + burst has slight risk during sustained spikes if burst capacity exhausted. Need clear fallback (lower-quality model) for graceful degradation.
zara: Autoscale tuning: scale-up threshold at queue latency >80ms sustained for 15s; scale-down after 4m idle. Set max autoscale step of +2 GPUs to avoid large coldstarts.
omar: KV/cache warmup: important. Recommend nightly warmup job for prompt prefixes and a pre-launch warmup before known campaigns. We can provide a warmup playbook and a small script: ```./warmup --profile meridian --replay last_24h```
lucas: Failure modes to include in presales doc: GPU OOM (mitigate via lower batch size + fallback model), AZ outage (route to other AZs + burst), cold KV cache (warmup + short-term degraded latency).
qa-bot: loadtest: meridian-sim completed  baseline 9gpu config @1800 qps, p95 gen 242ms (6B quant). Embedding throughput routed to cpu-service.
nina: Great. Can someone draft a one-page ops checklist and two pricing options (numbers are illustrative) so I can share with procurement tomorrow?
harry: I'll draft pricing: Option A (12 reserved): fixed $X/mo, Option B (9 reserved + burst): fixed lower $Y/mo + metered bursts at $Z/hr. I'll add SLA notes.
zara: I'll assemble the ops checklist and the short failure-modes table. Keep it <1 page.
nina: Perfect. @omar @lucas please add any compliance notes (KMS, VPC peering) for their security team.
omar: We have VPC peering + KMS for Dedicated. If they need full on-prem audit trail, offer Private eval. I'll state standard SOC2 bundle is available.
lucas: I'll attach brief diagram for routing: reserve pool -> burst pool -> fallback model.
nina: Thanks team 389 I'll send the consolidated doc to Meridian in the AM.
